title: Brazil Receives Parts for Two Quantum Computers in Partnership With China
html:
Insider Brief

  • Brazil received parts for two quantum computers under a partnership with Chinese technology company CETC that includes training for Brazilian researchers.
  • The shipment, valued at about $14.2 million, arrived in João Pessoa, where 15 Brazilian researchers are scheduled to begin assembly Nov. 24 under the supervision of Chinese specialists.
  • Testing is expected to begin in January 2027, with research projects set to start in the first half of the year.
  • Image: Mateus de Medeiros / Paraíba State Science and Technology Secretariat

Brazil received parts for two quantum computers under a deal with Chinese technology company China Electronics Technology Group Corporation, or CETC.

The equipment arrived Nov. 16 in João Pessoa, the capital of the northeastern state of Paraíba, Brazil’s Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation said in a news release. The ministry valued the shipment at about 83 million Brazilian reais — about $14.2 million — and described it as the most valuable cargo ever handled in a single container in the country. It traveled under escort from Recife at controlled speeds to Estação das Artes, the site of a new federal and state research center.

Assembly is scheduled to begin Nov. 24, with 15 Brazilian researchers working under the supervision of Chinese specialists. The contract calls for the Brazilian team to take part in assembly, configuration and maintenance. The ministry said the arrangement is intended to give Brazilian researchers the skills to operate and service the equipment and develop their own software for it.

The project brings together the federal science ministry, Paraíba’s government, the state’s science and technology secretariat, its research funding foundation and CETC. The machines will be housed at the International Center for Computing and Quantum Technologies, known as Ciquanta. The ministry said the center is part of a broader effort to expand Brazil’s advanced computing capacity in Latin America and build up research in the country’s Northeast.

Chinese specialists to oversee assembly

About 12 specialists from China are expected for the first stage of installation, the ministry said in the release. More will join beginning in January, bringing the number of visiting technicians involved in the project to about 25.

The installation team will start with the machines’ physical structure and cooling equipment. The cooling system maintains the extremely low temperatures the processors need to run. Quantum computers store information in units called qubits, which are sensitive to disturbances such as heat. The team will then set up the operating system and control software and connect the machines’ separate components, the ministry said.

The first adjustments are planned for December. Testing is expected to begin in January 2027, once imported materials needed for cooling arrive. The ministry listed nitrogen, helium-4 and helium-3 among those supplies and said helium-3 is in limited supply internationally.

Technicians will check that the machines work as intended before research begins. The ministry expects scientific projects to get underway during the first half of 2027.

Brazil seeks to build local expertise

Science and Technology Minister Luciana Santos said the project would train Brazilian researchers to develop their own algorithms. She said the goal was to build expertise that researchers could apply to practical problems and to direct more research funding to the Northeast, where the government hopes to retain scientists and engineers.

“We are decentralizing funding, strengthening advanced research, and creating opportunities in the Northeast to retain and project our greatest talents on the global stage”, Santos said, according to the rrelease.

Claudio Furtado, Paraíba’s science and technology secretary, said the agreement would help Brazil build the skills to operate the machines independently. Brazilian researchers have already traveled to China and participated in work on chip design and construction and on the cooling system, he said.

“It is a very important milestone for Brazil and for Paraíba, a milestone of sovereignty. We have entered the select group of ten countries with access to quantum technologies. And it’s not just two computers: beyond them, there’s technology transfer. Our researchers have already been to China and participated in several processes that will now be implemented here, such as the design and construction of the chip, the entire cooling part and the forming part”, Furtado said in the release.

Paraíba Gov. Lucas Ribeiro, who was present when the cargo arrived, said in the release that he expected the center to attract researchers, companies and investment. He said the facility would build on the state’s experience in scientific research and training.

“These two computers will be a game changer for science, technology and innovation in our state. We are bringing technology that will attract companies, researchers, and new investments, enabling the search for solutions that can improve people’s lives. Paraíba is already a reference in the training of professionals and scientific research, and is now taking another important step towards consolidating itself in this area”, Ribeiro said.

João Azevêdo, a former Paraíba governor and senator-elect who also attended the arrival, said the project had taken shape in less than two years, according to the news release. He said the center would expand opportunities for young researchers in Paraíba and add to Brazil’s research capacity.

“These two computers definitively place Paraíba on the world map for quantum computing research. It is an extraordinary achievement, built in less than two years, that will attract researchers, strengthen the training of our young people and expand Brazil’s scientific capacity. It is a project that goes beyond the borders of Paraíba and represents progress for the country”, Azevêdo said.

This story relies on an AI translation of the original press release in Portuguese.

Matt Swayne

MENTIONED IN THE ARTICLE

China Electronics Technology Group Corporation is a Chinese state-owned company. Its fields include communications equipment, computers, electronic equipment, IT infrastructure, networks, software development, research services, investment and asset management for civilian and military applications.
